views.name: department_degree_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT d.department_id, d.department_name, COUNT(dp.degree_program_id) AS degree_program_count FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON dp.department_id = d.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name
views.description: Per-department counts of degree programs (one row per department with department id, name, and number of degrees it offers).
validated_on: What is the name and id of the department with the most number of degrees ?
How many departments offer any degree?
How many different departments offer degrees?
counter_examples: How many degrees does the engineering department offer?

provenance.question: Which department offers the most number of degrees? List department name and id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the department that offers the largest number of degrees and return that department's name and id.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: Consider all departments present in the schema; count the number of degrees each department offers and select the department(s) with the maximum count.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (department_id, department_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT department_id, department_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM department_degree_counts GROUP BY department_id, department_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: degree_program_count matches COUNT of Degree_Programs per department (including zero via LEFT JOIN)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts v LEFT JOIN Departments d ON v.department_id = d.department_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Degree_Programs GROUP BY department_id) dp ON dp.department_id = v.department_id WHERE (COALESCE(dp.expected_count,0) != COALESCE(v.degree_program_count,0)) OR (d.department_id IS NULL)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL (department_id and department_name must be present)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts WHERE department_id IS NULL OR department_name IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Find the department that has the largest number of degrees and return that department's name and id.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: consider all departments; count degrees associated with each department and select the department(s) whose degree count is maximal
Sort/limit: order by degree count descending limit 1

Task: Count how many distinct departments offer any degree (i.e., the number of departments that have at least one degree associated with them).
Required outputs: an integer count equal to the number of departments that offer one or more degrees
Filters: Only include departments that are associated with at least one degree record (departments with zero associated degrees must be excluded)

Task: Compute the number of distinct departments that offer degrees.
Required outputs: a single numeric value representing the count of distinct departments that offer degrees
Filters: consider only rows where a department is associated with offering a degree; treat departments as distinct by their department identifier or name as present in the schema (count unique department values)
negative_subgoals:
Task: Count how many distinct degree programs are offered by the engineering department.
Required outputs: an integer count representing the number of degrees offered by the engineering department
Filters: department = 'engineering'; only include degree programs that are offered (exclude NULL/unknown offerings)

views.name: degrees_with_departments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Degree_Programs.degree_program_id,
  Degree_Programs.department_id AS degree_department_id,
  Degree_Programs.degree_summary_name,
  Degree_Programs.degree_summary_description,
  Degree_Programs.other_details AS degree_other_details,
  Departments.department_id AS dept_department_id,
  Departments.department_name,
  Departments.department_description,
  Departments.other_details AS dept_other_details
FROM Degree_Programs
LEFT JOIN Departments
  ON Degree_Programs.department_id = Departments.department_id
views.description: A denormalized relation listing degree programs along with their associated department details for joining or filtering by department

provenance.question: How many degrees does the engineering department have?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Count the number of degrees that belong to the engineering department.
Required outputs: count of degrees (an integer)
Filters: department equals 'engineering' (case-insensitive match)

tests.purpose: Each degree_program_id appears at most once in the view (no duplicate rows for the view's declared grain).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_program_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM degrees_with_departments GROUP BY degree_program_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view corresponds to an existing Degree_Programs row (no extra rows introduced by the JOIN).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degrees_with_departments v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs d ON v.degree_program_id = d.degree_program_id WHERE d.degree_program_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: degree_department_id in the view matches Degree_Programs.department_id and dept_department_id matches Departments.department_id when department exists (consistency of join columns and preservation of
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degrees_with_departments v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs d ON v.degree_program_id = d.degree_program_id LEFT JOIN Departments p ON d.department_id = p.department_id WHERE NOT (v.degree_department_id IS d.department_id) OR NOT ( (p.department_id IS NULL AND v.dept_department_id IS NULL) OR (p.department_id IS NOT NULL AND v.dept_department_id = p.department_id) )

views.name: courses_with_section_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, COUNT(s.section_id) AS section_count
FROM Courses c
LEFT JOIN Sections s ON s.course_id = c.course_id
GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name
views.description: Per-course counts of associated sections (includes courses with zero sections) providing course id, name, and section count for reuse in filters or joins.
counter_examples: What are the names and ids of every course with less than 2 sections?

provenance.question: What are the names and id of courses having at most 2 sections?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find all courses that have at most 2 sections and return each course's name and id.
Required outputs: course id; course name
Filters: include only courses whose count of associated sections is <= 2; if a course has zero sections it should be included (0 <= 2)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (course_id, course_name): detect courses that appear more than once in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT course_id, course_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM courses_with_section_counts GROUP BY course_id, course_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: section_count matches count of Sections per course (including zero) computed from base tables
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses_with_section_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT c.course_id, COUNT(s.section_id) AS expected_count FROM Courses c LEFT JOIN Sections s ON s.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id) b ON v.course_id = b.course_id WHERE v.section_count IS NOT b.expected_count OR (v.section_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (v.section_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL)

tests.purpose: Every course in Courses appears in the view (LEFT JOIN preserved rows): detect courses missing from the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Courses c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM courses_with_section_counts v WHERE v.course_id = c.course_id AND (v.course_name = c.course_name OR (v.course_name IS NULL AND c.course_name IS NULL)))

negative_subgoals:
Task: Return the course names and course ids for every course that has fewer than 2 sections associated with it.
Required outputs: course name; course id
Filters: Include only courses whose count of associated sections is less than 2 (i.e., 0 or 1 sections).; Treat 'sections' as the set of section records linked to a course via whatever course-to-section relationship exists in the schema.

views.name: semester_registration_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) AS registration_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id
views.description: Per-semester counts of student registrations (one row per semester with semester_id and registration_count) useful for ranking or filtering semesters by enrollment size.

provenance.question: What is the semester which most student registered in? Show both the name and the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the semester (its name and its id) that has the largest number of student registrations.
Required outputs: semester name; semester id
Filters: Consider all registrations of students across all semesters; count how many students are registered in each semester and select the semester with the maximum count. If multiple semesters tie for the maximum, return all tied semesters.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain: ensure semester_id is unique in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts v JOIN (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) AS c FROM semester_registration_counts GROUP BY semester_id HAVING c > 1) dup USING (semester_id)

tests.purpose: registration_count matches count of Student_Enrolment rows per semester
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id) s USING (semester_id) WHERE v.registration_count IS NOT (s.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL: semester_id must be non-NULL for every row
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts WHERE semester_id IS NULL

views.name: enrolments_per_student_per_semester
views.body_sql: SELECT se.semester_id, sem.semester_name AS semester, se.student_id, COUNT(*) AS student_registrations_per_student FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Semesters sem ON se.semester_id = sem.semester_id GROUP BY se.semester_id, sem.semester_name, se.student_id
views.description: Per-semester per-student counts of enrolment records (number of enrolments a student has in each semester) with semester labels and ids, useful for cohort and ranking queries.

provenance.question: For each semester, what is the name and id of the one with the most students registered?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: For each semester, find the single student registration record that has the largest number of students registered and return that semester together with that record's student name and student id.
Required outputs: semester; student name; student id
Filters: Consider each distinct semester value separately.; For each semester include only the record(s) whose count of students registered is maximal for that semester.; If there are ties for the maximum number of students in a semester, include the tied records (i.e., all student name and id values that share the maximum count for that semester).
Sort/limit: Order rows by semester in ascending order; no overall row limit.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (semester_id, semester, student_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, semester, student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM enrolments_per_student_per_semester GROUP BY semester_id, semester, student_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Measure student_registrations_per_student equals count of underlying Student_Enrolment rows for that (semester_id, student_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.semester_id, v.student_id FROM enrolments_per_student_per_semester v LEFT JOIN (SELECT semester_id, student_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_cnt FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id, student_id) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id AND v.student_id = b.student_id WHERE (b.expected_cnt IS NULL AND (v.student_registrations_per_student IS NOT NULL AND v.student_registrations_per_student <> 0)) OR (b.expected_cnt IS NOT NULL AND v.student_registrations_per_student <> b.expected_cnt))

tests.purpose: semester_id and student_id (keys) are not NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrolments_per_student_per_semester WHERE semester_id IS NULL OR student_id IS NULL

views.name: student_semester_degree_program_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT degree_program_id) AS distinct_degree_program_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id, semester_id
views.description: Per-student per-semester counts of distinct degree programs the student is enrolled in (one row per student and semester)
counter_examples: What are the first, middle, and last names, along with the ids, of all students who enrolled in 2 degree programs in one semester?

provenance.question: Who are enrolled in 2 degree programs in one semester? List the first name, middle name and last name and the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find students who are enrolled in exactly two degree programs during the same single semester; return their personal name parts and identifier.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id
Filters: count of distinct degree-program enrollments for a given student must equal 2 within the same semester (i.e., same semester identifier); include only rows where the two enrollments occur in the same semester value (exact match); exclude students with fewer or more than 2 degree-program enrollments in that semester

tests.purpose: View has exactly one row per (student_id, semester_id) — detect duplicate keys in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts GROUP BY student_id, semester_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: distinct_degree_program_count equals the count of distinct degree_program_id in base table for that student & semester
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT degree_program_id) AS expected_cnt FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id, semester_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id AND v.semester_id = b.semester_id WHERE (b.expected_cnt IS NULL AND v.distinct_degree_program_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_cnt IS NOT NULL AND v.distinct_degree_program_count <> b.expected_cnt)

tests.purpose: No NULLs in the key columns student_id or semester_id in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts WHERE student_id IS NULL OR semester_id IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: Return the first name, middle name, last name, and id for every student who, within a single semester, enrolled in exactly two distinct degree programs.
Required outputs: student first name; student middle name; student last name; student id
Filters: Include only students for whom there exists at least one semester in which that student enrolled in exactly 2 distinct degree programs (count distinct degree programs per student per semester = 2).; If a student enrolled in 2 programs in multiple semesters, include that student only once (one row per student).; Do not include students who never had any semester with exactly 2 distinct degree programs (exclude counts other than 2).

views.name: students_enrolled_in_degree_programs
views.body_sql: SELECT se.student_enrolment_id, se.student_id, se.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id
views.description: A relation listing student identifiers joined to their enrolment and degree program identifiers and degree program summary name, useful to get cohorts of students by program type.

provenance.question: What are the first, middle, and last names for everybody enrolled in a Bachelors program?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Retrieve the first name, middle name, and last name for every person who is enrolled in a Bachelors program.
Required outputs: first name: the person's given/first name; middle name: the person's middle name (if any); last name: the person's family/last name
Filters: enrollment program equals 'Bachelors' (case-insensitive match); include a row for every person currently enrolled in a Bachelors program; do not include people in other program types or unenrolled people

tests.purpose: Enforcement of grain: student_enrolment_id must be unique (no duplicate rows for the key).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_enrolment_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students_enrolled_in_degree_programs GROUP BY student_enrolment_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Join integrity: every row's degree_program_id must exist in Degree_Programs (the view should not introduce rows with missing degree program FK).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_enrolled_in_degree_programs v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON v.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE dp.degree_program_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: Reconciliation of degree_summary_name: degree_summary_name in the view must match Degree_Programs.degree_summary_name for the referenced degree_program_id.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_enrolled_in_degree_programs v JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON v.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id WHERE (v.degree_summary_name IS NOT dp.degree_summary_name) AND NOT (v.degree_summary_name IS NULL AND dp.degree_summary_name IS NULL)

views.name: program_kind_student_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind,
       COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS student_count
FROM "Degree_Programs" dp
JOIN "Student_Enrolment" se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id
GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per-program-kind counts of distinct students enrolled in degree programs (denormalized cohort size by program kind).

provenance.question: Find the kind of program which most number of students are enrolled in?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Determine which program kind has the largest number of enrolled students and return that program kind along with its student count.
Required outputs: program_kind - the kind/type/category of program; student_count - the number of students enrolled in programs of that kind
Filters: Include only records that represent currently enrolled students (no filter specified in question: interpret as all student enrollments present in the data).; Count all students associated with programs grouped by program kind.
Sort/limit: order by student_count desc limit 1

tests.purpose: View has one row per program_kind (no duplicate program_kind values)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT program_kind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM program_kind_student_counts GROUP BY program_kind HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: student_count equals distinct count of student_id from base tables for that program_kind
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.program_kind FROM program_kind_student_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS expected_count FROM Degree_Programs dp JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.program_kind = b.program_kind WHERE (v.student_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (v.student_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL) OR (v.student_count <> b.expected_count))

tests.purpose: Every program_kind key in the view is NOT NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM program_kind_student_counts WHERE program_kind IS NULL

views.name: degree_summary_enrolment_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS number_of_students FROM Degree_Programs dp LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: For each degree_summary_name, the count of student enrolment records associated with degree programs having that summary name (includes zero via left join)

provenance.question: What is the degree summary name that has the most number of students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the degree summary name that has the largest number of students enrolled.
Required outputs: degree_summary_name; number_of_students
Filters: Consider all records of student enrollments across degree summary names; Count each student enrollment toward the corresponding degree summary name; Include degree summary names with zero enrollments only if they are present in the data and could tie for the maximum
Sort/limit: order by number_of_students desc limit 1

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (degree_summary_name). Ensures view has at most one row per degree_summary_name.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM degree_summary_enrolment_counts GROUP BY degree_summary_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: number_of_students matches recomputed COUNT of Student_Enrolment rows per degree_summary_name using the base tables (including zero via LEFT JOIN).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.degree_summary_name FROM degree_summary_enrolment_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS expected_count FROM Degree_Programs dp LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.degree_summary_name = b.degree_summary_name WHERE (v.number_of_students IS NULL AND (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count != 0)) OR (v.number_of_students IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL) OR (v.number_of_students IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.number_of_students != b.expected_count))

tests.purpose: degree_summary_name (the key) is never NULL in the view.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_summary_enrolment_counts WHERE degree_summary_name IS NULL

views.name: degree_program_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT dp.degree_program_id, COALESCE(se.student_count, 0) AS student_count
FROM Degree_Programs dp
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT degree_program_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) AS student_count
  FROM Student_Enrolment
  GROUP BY degree_program_id
) se ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id
views.description: Per-degree-program counts of distinct enrolled students, including programs with zero enrollments

provenance.question: Find the program which most number of students are enrolled in. List both the id and the summary.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the program that has the largest number of enrolled students and return that program's id and its summary.
Required outputs: program id; program summary
Filters: Consider all programs and count how many students are enrolled in each program. If multiple programs are tied for the maximum number of enrolled students, return all such programs.; Do not filter out any programs by status or date; include programs with zero or more enrolled students.
Sort/limit: No specific ordering required; return all program rows whose enrolled-student count equals the maximum count (no row limit).

tests.purpose: View has one row per degree_program_id in Degree_Programs (no missing programs)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Degree_Programs dp WHERE dp.degree_program_id NOT IN (SELECT degree_program_id FROM degree_program_enrollment_counts)

tests.purpose: student_count equals COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) from Student_Enrolment for that degree_program_id (reconciles measure)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_program_enrollment_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT degree_program_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY degree_program_id) se ON v.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id WHERE v.student_count != COALESCE(se.expected_count, 0)

tests.purpose: degree_program_id is never NULL in the view (key non-null)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_program_enrollment_counts v WHERE v.degree_program_id IS NULL

views.name: degree_program_enrollment_counts_12
views.body_sql:
SELECT dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS enrollment_count
FROM Degree_Programs dp
JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id
GROUP BY dp.degree_program_id, dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per-degree-program counts of enrolled students (one row per degree program with at least one enrollment) useful for comparing or filtering programs by enrollment size.

provenance.question: What is the program id and the summary of the degree that has the most students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the program id and the summary of the degree for the degree program that has the highest number of enrolled students.
Required outputs: program id (the identifier of the degree program); degree summary (the textual summary/description of that degree)
Filters: Consider only degree programs that have one or more students enrolled; Select the degree program(s) whose enrolled student count is maximal (i.e., no other degree has a larger enrolled student count)
Sort/limit: If multiple degree programs tie for the highest enrolled student count, return all of them; otherwise return the single top program. No additional ordering is required.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows for the declared grain (degree_program_id, degree_summary_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_program_id, degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM degree_program_enrollment_counts_12 GROUP BY degree_program_id, degree_summary_name HAVING cnt > 1) AS t

tests.purpose: Each enrollment_count equals the count of Student_Enrolment rows that reference that degree_program_id (verifies aggregation correctness).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_program_enrollment_counts_12 v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp USING(degree_program_id) WHERE v.enrollment_count != (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Student_Enrolment se WHERE se.degree_program_id = v.degree_program_id)

tests.purpose: Every row's degree_program_id and degree_summary_name correspond to an existing Degree_Programs row (no orphaned keys / join didn't fabricate rows).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM degree_program_enrollment_counts_12 v LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON v.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id AND (v.degree_summary_name IS dp.degree_summary_name OR (v.degree_summary_name IS NULL AND dp.degree_summary_name IS NULL)) WHERE dp.degree_program_id IS NULL

views.name: student_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.middle_name, s.last_name, COUNT(se.student_enrolment_id) AS enrollment_count FROM Students s LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.middle_name, s.last_name
views.description: Per-student total count of enrollment records, with student identifying fields for joins and reporting.

provenance.question: Which student has enrolled for the most times in any program? List the id, first name, middle name, last name, the number of enrollments and student id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the student or students who have the highest number of enrollments in any program, and report identifying information and that enrollment count.
Required outputs: id (the student's id); first name; middle name; last name; the number of enrollments (how many times that student enrolled in any program); student id (same as id if schema uses 'student id' separately; include both as requested)
Filters: Consider all enrollment records for all programs and all students; Count enrollments per student across all programs (no time range restriction); Return only the student(s) whose enrollment count equals the maximum enrollment count among all students
Sort/limit: No specific ordering required; limit to only those rows whose enrollment count equals the maximum (no numeric limit unless multiple students tie)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts v JOIN (SELECT student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_enrollment_counts GROUP BY student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name HAVING cnt > 1) d ON v.student_id = d.student_id AND (v.first_name IS d.first_name OR (v.first_name IS NOT NULL AND d.first_name IS NOT NULL AND v.first_name = d.first_name)) AND (v.middle_name IS d.middle_name OR (v.middle_name IS NOT NULL AND d.middle_name IS NOT NULL AND v.middle_name = d.middle_name)) AND (v.last_name IS d.last_name OR (v.last_name IS NOT NULL AND d.last_name IS NOT NULL AND v.last_name = d.last_name))

tests.purpose: Each enrollment_count equals the count of Student_Enrolment rows for that student (reconciliation with base table)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, COUNT(student_enrolment_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrollment_count != 0) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrollment_count != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Key fields are not NULL (student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name) for every row
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts v WHERE v.student_id IS NULL OR v.first_name IS NULL OR v.middle_name IS NULL OR v.last_name IS NULL

views.name: student_program_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT student_id, degree_program_id, COUNT(*) AS enrol_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id, degree_program_id
views.description: Per-student per-program enrollment counts (one row per student and degree program with the count of enrollments).

provenance.question: What is the first, middle, and last name, along with the id and number of enrollments, for the student who enrolled the most in any program?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the student who has the maximum number of enrollments in any single program and return that student's first name, middle name, last name, id, and the number of enrollments (the maximum enrollments count for that student in a single program).
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id; number of enrollments
Filters: consider enrollment counts grouped by student and program; select the student-program group with the highest enrollment count across all students and programs; if multiple student-program groups tie for the maximum count, return all tied students with their respective names, ids, and that maximum enrollment count
Sort/limit: no particular ordering required; limit to rows that have the maximum enrollment count (i.e., global maximum)

params.when_to_use: Identify students whose registered permanent address differs from their current address. | Join to address details when you need only students who have two distinct address references. | As a filter/input when downstream logic should only consider students with non-null student_id and distinct address ids.

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_release_dates v LEFT JOIN Transcripts t ON v.transcript_id = t.transcript_id WHERE v.transcript_id IS NULL OR (t.transcript_id IS NOT NULL AND t.transcript_date IS NULL)

views.name: student_course_transcript_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT sec.student_course_id, COUNT(DISTINCT tc.transcript_id) AS distinct_transcript_count FROM Student_Enrolment_Courses sec JOIN Transcript_Contents tc ON tc.student_course_id = sec.student_course_id GROUP BY sec.student_course_id
views.description: Per student_course (course enrollment) the count of distinct transcripts in which that student_course appears
validated_on: What is the maximum number of times that a course shows up in different transcripts and what is that course's enrollment id?

provenance.question: How many times at most can a course enrollment result show in different transcripts? Also show the course enrollment id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find, for each course enrollment id, the maximum number of different transcripts in which that course enrollment appears, and report the course enrollment id together with that maximum count.
Required outputs: course enrollment id; maximum number of distinct transcripts in which that course enrollment appears
Filters: consider all course enrollment records in the database with any associated transcript entries; count distinct transcripts per course enrollment (do not deduplicate by other attributes); include only course enrollments that appear in at least one transcript
Sort/limit: order results by course enrollment id ascending; no row limit

tests.purpose: Every row in the view has a non-NULL student_course_id (key not NULL)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_course_transcript_counts WHERE student_course_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: distinct_transcript_count equals count of distinct Transcript_Contents.transcript_id for that student_course_id (measure reconciles with base tables)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_course_transcript_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_course_id AS scid, COUNT(DISTINCT transcript_id) AS expected_cnt FROM Transcript_Contents GROUP BY student_course_id) b ON v.student_course_id = b.scid WHERE (b.expected_cnt IS NULL AND v.distinct_transcript_count != 0) OR (b.expected_cnt IS NOT NULL AND v.distinct_transcript_count != b.expected_cnt)

tests.purpose: View does not contain student_course_id values that do not exist in Student_Enrolment_Courses (no phantom keys introduced)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_course_transcript_counts v LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses s ON v.student_course_id = s.student_course_id WHERE s.student_course_id IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Find the course (identified by its enrollment id) that appears the maximum number of times across different transcripts, and report that maximum count and the corresponding enrollment id.
Required outputs: enrollment id of the course that appears most often across transcripts; the maximum number of transcript rows in which that enrollment id appears
Filters: consider all transcript records in the transcripts dataset (no additional filtering); count occurrences per enrollment id treating each transcript row as one occurrence
Sort/limit: order by the count descending and return the top 1 (limit 1)

views.name: transcript_content_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT tc.transcript_id, COUNT(*) AS number_of_results FROM Transcript_Contents tc GROUP BY tc.transcript_id
views.description: Per-transcript counts of related Transcript_Contents rows (number of content items per transcript), useful for queries comparing or filtering transcripts by their content counts.

provenance.question: Show the date of the transcript which shows the least number of results, also list the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the transcript date(s) and corresponding id(s) for the transcript(s) that have the smallest numeric value in the 'number of results' field.
Required outputs: transcript date; id
Filters: consider all transcripts; compute the minimum value of the 'number of results' field across all transcripts and return only rows whose 'number of results' equals that minimum (i.e., the transcript(s) with the least number of results)

tests.purpose: No NULL transcript_id keys (every row in the view must have a non-NULL transcript_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_content_counts WHERE transcript_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: number_of_results equals the count of Transcript_Contents rows for that transcript_id (measure reconciles with base table)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_content_counts v WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Transcript_Contents tc WHERE tc.transcript_id = v.transcript_id) != v.number_of_results

tests.purpose: View contains no transcript_ids not present in base table grouping (every row in view must correspond to at least one Transcript_Contents row)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_content_counts v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Transcript_Contents tc WHERE tc.transcript_id = v.transcript_id)

views.name: transcript_results_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date, COUNT(tc.student_course_id) AS results FROM Transcripts t LEFT JOIN Transcript_Contents tc ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id GROUP BY t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date
views.description: Per-transcript count of associated transcript_content rows (number of results) with transcript id and date, excluding no rows filtering

provenance.question: What is the date and id of the transcript with the least number of results?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the transcript row that has the smallest value in its 'results' field and return that transcript's 'date' and 'id'.
Required outputs: date; id
Filters: consider only rows where 'results' is not NULL; if multiple transcripts tie for the smallest 'results' value, return all tied transcript rows' date and id
Sort/limit: order by results ascending; no fixed row limit (return all ties for the minimum)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (transcript_id, transcript_date)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transcript_results_counts GROUP BY transcript_id, transcript_date HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row's results equals the count of Transcript_Contents rows for that transcript_id (recomputed measure)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_results_counts trc LEFT JOIN Transcripts t ON t.transcript_id = trc.transcript_id WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Transcript_Contents tc WHERE tc.transcript_id = trc.transcript_id) IS NOT trc.results

tests.purpose: All key columns are NOT NULL (transcript_id and transcript_date must be present)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_results_counts WHERE transcript_id IS NULL OR transcript_date IS NULL

views.name: semester_degree_level_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT SE.semester_id, Sem.semester_name, DP.degree_summary_name AS degree_level, COUNT(*) AS enrolment_count
FROM Student_Enrolment SE
JOIN Degree_Programs DP ON SE.degree_program_id = DP.degree_program_id
JOIN Semesters Sem ON SE.semester_id = Sem.semester_id
GROUP BY SE.semester_id, Sem.semester_name, DP.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per-semester counts of enrolled students broken down by degree-level (as recorded on the degree program), useful to know which semesters have enrollments for particular degree levels.

provenance.question: Find the semester when both Master students and Bachelor students got enrolled in.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Identify the semester(s) in which both Master students and Bachelor students were enrolled.
Required outputs: semester
Filters: Include only semesters for which there exists at least one enrolled student whose degree level is 'Master' and at least one enrolled student whose degree level is 'Bachelor'.; Treat 'Master' and 'Bachelor' as the exact degree-level string values to match.

tests.purpose: Detect duplicate rows in the view's declared grain (semester_id, semester_name, degree_level)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, semester_name, degree_level, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semester_degree_level_counts GROUP BY semester_id, semester_name, degree_level HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Verify enrolment_count matches count of Student_Enrolment rows for that semester and degree_level (degree_program -> degree_summary_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_degree_level_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT SE.semester_id, DP.degree_summary_name AS degree_level, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment SE JOIN Degree_Programs DP ON SE.degree_program_id = DP.degree_program_id GROUP BY SE.semester_id, DP.degree_summary_name) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id AND v.degree_level = b.degree_level WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrolment_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrolment_count != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Ensure key columns are NOT NULL in the view (semester_id, semester_name, degree_level)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_degree_level_counts WHERE semester_id IS NULL OR semester_name IS NULL OR degree_level IS NULL

views.name: semester_enrolment_degree_summary_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_enrolment_id) AS enrolment_count
FROM Student_Enrolment se
JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id
GROUP BY se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per-semester counts of enrolments broken down by student degree_summary_name (e.g., Masters, Bachelors), useful to determine which semesters have enrolments from multiple degree levels.

provenance.question: What is the id of the semester that had both Masters and Bachelors students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the semester id for the semester(s) in which both at least one Masters student and at least one Bachelors student were enrolled.
Required outputs: semester id
Filters: Consider enrollment records and student degree levels; count a semester if there exists at least one enrollment for a student whose degree level is 'Masters' and at least one enrollment for a student whose degree level is 'Bachelors' in the same semester; Only semesters meeting both conditions should be returned

tests.purpose: View has correct grain: no duplicate rows for same (semester_id, degree_summary_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semester_enrolment_degree_summary_counts GROUP BY semester_id, degree_summary_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: enrolment_count matches COUNT(DISTINCT student_enrolment_id) from base tables after the same join and grouping
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.semester_id, v.degree_summary_name FROM semester_enrolment_degree_summary_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_enrolment_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id AND v.degree_summary_name = b.degree_summary_name WHERE (v.enrolment_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (v.enrolment_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL) OR (v.enrolment_count <> b.expected_count))

tests.purpose: All key columns in the view are NOT NULL (semester_id and degree_summary_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_enrolment_degree_summary_counts WHERE semester_id IS NULL OR degree_summary_name IS NULL
